item.title: Carrick to remain Man Utd boss for Chelsea clash – Reports
item.description: Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United for this weekend’s Premier League match away to Chelsea, according to media reports on Tuesday. Carrick’s future as United manager has been the subject of intense speculation after a run of eight games without a win. Sunday’s 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth left the English giants just one point above the Premier League relegation zone. But the BBC, Sky Sports and Britain’s Press Association all reported that former United and England midfielder Carrick would take the team to Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Carrick arrived at United’s Carrington training ground on Tuesday to oversee a routine squad session. The BBC cited “sources” as saying the 45-year-old would be given a chance by the United hierarchy to turn things around at Old Trafford following a terrible start to the season. Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after overseeing an impressive revival as caretaker boss following United’s struggles under Ruben Amorim. The club recovered to finish third in the Premier League, earning a return to the Champions League. item.title: Tinubu directs security agencies to arrest killers of Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has directed the Nigeria Police and other relevant security agencies to move swiftly and ensure that those behind the murder of prominent Islamic preacher Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka and his friend, Adamu Abubakar, in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, are apprehended and brought to justice. President Tinubu also condemned the dastardly act, describing it as heinous and an assault on the values of peace and the sanctity of human life. The gunmen killed the two men in a drive-by shooting on Monday evening. A statement by the presidential spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, said: “The President, who was deeply saddened by the news of the killing, described the act as heinous and an assault on the values of peace and the sanctity of human life.” He extended his heartfelt condolences to the families of the deceased, their followers, and the government and people of Katsina State over the tragic loss. According to the statement: “The President has directed the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security agencies to move swiftly, intensify efforts already underway by the Katsina State Police Command, and ensure the perpetrators are tracked down, apprehended, and brought to justice. “President Tinubu prays for the repose of the souls of the departed and for comfort for all those who mourn their deaths.” The post Tinubu directs security agencies to arrest killers of Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Edo Voter Register: Utomi, others demand INEC explanation over alleged AI-generated images
item.description: By Emmanuel Okogba Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) chieftain and economist, Prof. Pat Utomi, has raised concerns over allegations that artificial intelligence (AI)-generated photographs appear in the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) online voter register in parts of Edo State. Utomi’s reaction followed posts by social media user Decosule, who called on INEC to explain the presence of what he described as AI-generated images in voter records displayed on the commission’s website. Decosule shared screenshots purportedly taken from the online voter register for polling units in Ward 11, Etsako West Local Government Area, and Udomi in Esan Central Local Government Area, questioning the authenticity of some photographs. He asked the electoral commission to clarify how the images were included in the register, who conducted the voter registration or image-capturing process, and whether the Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) associated with the entries had been collected. In a post reacting to the issue, Utomi warned that questions surrounding the images could undermine public confidence in the country’s electoral process if not properly addressed. “INEC cannot afford to be careless with the credibility of Nigeria’s electoral process. The presence of AI-generated images in a register meant to support our democracy raises serious questions about verification, transparency and accountability. Our democracy is at stake here!” Utomi wrote. Decosule had also claimed to have observed similar images in the register for Udomi in Esan Central, the local government area associated with Edo State Governor Monday Okpebholo. The screenshots shared by Decosule showed voter entries under polling units identified as Iyoku–Utukwe Afashio Booth and Ikabigbo I–Ikabigbo Primary School in Etsako West, as well as Udomi Primary School in Esan Central. Decosule urged INEC to provide an explanation, particularly regarding the origin of the photographs and the processes used to verify voter information. However, the screenshots alone do not independently establish that the images were generated using AI or demonstrate whether any irregularities occurred during voter registration. INEC is yet to provide an official response to clarify the authenticity of the photographs, how they came to appear on the online platform and whether the commission had identified any problems with the records. item.description: Kylian Mbappe apologised on Tuesday after the Real Madrid star was dropped by major Chinese brands for apparently joking about Mao Zedong in a video that has gone viral. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. “My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. item.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval to expand transfer of convicted offenders agreements
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina President Bola Tinubu has transmitted a bill seeking to amend the Transfer of Convicted Offenders (Enactment and Enforcement) Act to the House of Representatives for consideration, with a view to extending its application to countries outside the Commonwealth. In a letter dated October 20, 2026, addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, Tinubu urged lawmakers to consider the proposed legislation expeditiously. The bill, titled Transfer of Convicted Offenders (Enactment and Enforcement) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeks to amend the existing law, Cap. T16, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. According to the President, the proposed amendment is designed to give effect to schemes or agreements between the Federal Government of Nigeria and other countries for the transfer of convicted offenders. The amendment would also empower the President, through an order published in the Federal Gazette, to extend the application of the Act to any country with which Nigeria has entered into such an agreement. Tinubu said the proposed change would enable Nigeria to implement agreements concluded with countries outside the Commonwealth, potentially broadening the scope of international cooperation on the transfer of convicted offenders. Transmitting the bill pursuant to Section 58(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the President formally requested the consideration of the House of Representatives. “While it is my hope that the House of Representatives will consider this submission expeditiously, please accept, Rt. Hon. Speaker, the assurances of my highest consideration,” Tinubu stated in the letter. The bill is now before the House for consideration. The presidential communication did not specify the countries that could be covered by future agreements or provide details of the proposed implementation arrangements. This was contained in a letter by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume which was read on the floor of the House during plenary in Abuja. item.title: Maresca defends Donnarumma, Guehi after Man City defeat
item.description: Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca on Tuesday defended goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and centre-back Marc Guehi after costly mistakes in their first Premier League defeat of the season at Aston Villa. Nicolas Jackson took advantage of errors from the pair as Villa won 2-1 on Saturday, ending City’s perfect run of seven wins from seven league games. Defeat left City level on points with champions Arsenal at the top of the table, but they are ahead of the Gunners on goal difference. Maresca spoke up for his players ahead of a tough League Cup fourth-round match against Brighton at the Etihad on Wednesday. “Gigio (Donnarumma), I think, since we started, is doing well. Like any player, like any manager, at some point is making some mistakes. “But it’s part of the season. Again, they are playing so many games, so many minutes, that sometimes it’s almost impossible to (not) make some mistakes.” And Maresca said he was “completely happy” with England defender Guehi. “Because in the way he reacts, he’s fantastic, he’s a top guy,” he said. “Again, he’s one of the captains, he’s a leader, and I love Marc, to be honest. “And again, it’s the same with Gigio — when they make some mistakes, they recognise.” Maresca said Donnarumma was among a group of players who had been given time off to recharge after the Villa defeat, also including Erling Haaland, Elliot Anderson, Josko Gvardiol and captain Ruben Dias. “After Villa, we gave five players three days off to recover energy — Erling, Ruben, Elliot, Gigio and Josko,” he said. “They are all on holiday.” AFP The post Maresca defends Donnarumma, Guehi after Man City defeat appeared first on Vanguard News .

KNN’s reaction followed Ike-Muonso’s recent call on Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, to drop his ambition and support Tinubu in 2027, arguing that the South should complete its eight-year tenure before power returns to the North. item.title: Venus Williams suffers 16th defeat in a row with loss to teenager
item.description: Venus Williams suffered her 16th loss in a row in singles tennis as the 46-year-old American icon was defeated by teenager Lilli Tagger in straight sets at the Guangzhou Open on Tuesday. Austria’s Tagger, who is 28 years younger than the former world number one, eased through 6-2, 6-2 in southern China. Williams, a seven-time Grand Slam singles champion, last won a singles match on the WTA Tour in July last year. Now ranked 599 in the world, Williams last played at the US Open in August-September, when she lost in the first round in straight sets to Sofia Kenin. Williams won in the doubles with Indonesia’s Janice Tjen in Guangzhou on Monday. They will play again on Wednesday. The 53rd-ranked Tagger faces Magda Linette of Poland in the next round. item.title: Ronaldo in line for Portugal return after fallout with coach
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo is in Portugal’s preliminary squad for next month’s Nations League matches, opening the door to an international return after his fallout with coach Jorge Jesus, a federation source told AFP on Tuesday. The 41-year-old abruptly left the Portugal camp on September 30 during the opening qualifiers for the Nations League, before accusing Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time. You do not even need to dig into staff and digital infrastructure support costs to see that burning money in the budget race is an unsustainable strategy, even short-term. A positive gaming experience, paying winners on time and solving their problems builds our brand reputation and reduces churn [percentage of players who stop depositing and betting over a specific time period, usually measured in periods between 7 and 90 days] . Fail their trust — and funds invested in CAC are gone with your reputation. Helabet is all about building trust by giving players exactly what we promised during sign-up. This is the policy we have entered the Nigerian iGaming market with. Or any other African market we operate in. But in the new circumstances, we chose to double down on this policy. And redirected even more money from marketing into customer experience assets: bonuses, localisation, our team, payouts… Oh yes, Nigerian bettors have some very public arguments about not getting their winnings. This might sound new to some, but often sportsbooks withhold payments because they lack sufficient operational balance to suddenly pay out a large single win or a volume of winning bets placed on a high-odds event. And they fail to notice that even a single complaint going viral over tens of thousands on social media from a customer denied their legitimate funds will destroy their previous marketing investments. And trust. So continuing to build and protect trust with our players by paying out winnings on time is our best bet, pun intended. That is why part of our funds went into operational balance. So any bettor at Helabet could be assured that if they legitimately win a large sum, they will promptly receive their money upon request. But paying winners is a bookmaker’s basic obligation. item.title: Six times English players won Ballon d’Or
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Harry Kane has joined an exclusive group of English footballers to have won the prestigious Ballon d’Or, becoming the fifth Englishman to claim the men’s award after his remarkable 2025/26 campaign with Bayern Munich and England. The England captain scored 73 goals for club and country last season, ending a 25-year wait for an English winner following Michael Owen’s triumph in 2001. Here are the English players who have won the Ballon d’Or and the years they claimed football’s prestigious individual honour. Sir Stanley Matthews (1956) The legendary Blackpool winger became the first-ever Ballon d’Or winner when he received the award in 1956. Known for his exceptional dribbling skills and ability to beat defenders, Matthews made history at the age of 41, a record that still makes him the oldest winner of the award. Sir Bobby Charlton (1966) Charlton won the Ballon d’Or in the same year England lifted their first and only FIFA World Cup title. The Manchester United legend played a key role in the Three Lions’ triumph on home soil, scoring three goals during the tournament, including two in the semi-final victory over Portugal. Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) Keegan became the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or in consecutive years. He claimed the award in 1978 and retained it in 1979 while playing for German side Hamburg. His performances in Germany established him as one of the leading footballers of his generation. Michael Owen (2001) Owen became the fourth Englishman to win the award after an outstanding year with Liverpool. He helped the club secure the FA Cup, League Cup and UEFA Cup in the 2000/01 season, scoring crucial goals along the way. His speed, finishing and memorable performances for club and country helped him beat the competition for the award. Harry Kane (2026) Kane became the fifth Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or after an extraordinary season with Bayern Munich and England. His 73 goals across 65 appearances helped Bayern win the Bundesliga, DFB Pokal and Franz Beckenbauer Supercup. He also helped England finish third at the 2026 World Cup, their best result since winning the tournament in 1966. Kane’s triumph ended the long wait for another English winner and placed him alongside some of the biggest names in the country’s football history. A record worth noting: Although five Englishmen have won the award, Kevin Keegan remains the only English player to have won it twice in consecutive years. Kane is the latest addition to a list that stretches back seven decades. Vanguard News The post Six times English players won Ballon d’Or appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UK to charge varsities $1,200 per Nigerian, other foreign student from 2028
item.description: …Targets $594m revenue in first year By Nkiruka Nnorom & Marvellous Chukwunenye Universities in England will now have to pay an annual levy of £925 ($1,200) for each international student beyond an exemption threshold from August 2028, in a move targeting institutions enrolling students from Nigeria, China, Pakistan, India and Bangladesh. The policy, first announced in the UK government’s 2025 budget, was reaffirmed by the Education Minister, Josh MacAlister, who asserted that the revenue would support England’s higher education and skills system. The fresh levy, according to the Department of Education, covers both new and existing students. MacAlister noted that the government had conducted consultations and published an impact assessment in 2025, with an updated analysis expected shortly. He maintained that a planned increase in domestic tuition fee caps could generate about £6 billion for providers over five years, compared with the levy’s projected cost of less than £1 billion. Under the proposal, universities will pay £925 annually for each international student, with the first 220 overseas enrolments exempted. The Office for Students will oversee implementation using enrolment data. Government projects the levy will generate £445 million ($594 million) in 2028-2029, with the figure rising to £480 million ($641 million) by 2030-2031. Home Office figures showed that Nigeria received 26,060 sponsored study visas in the year ending June 2026, behind China with 86,368 and India with 82,523. Pakistan recorded 19,600, while Bangladesh got about 8,800. For Nigerian students, who form one of UK’s largest international cohorts, the charge could translate to higher tuition. The Department for Education data further showed that Nigerian students generated £1.7 billion in UK higher education export revenue in 2024, compared with £5.3 billion from India and £4.9 billion from China. Overall, international students generated an estimated £23.9 billion. Birmingham City University has already raised fees for continuing international students by 2 per cent for 2026-2027, with further 3.5 per cent planned for 2027-2028. The University of Bath has advised overseas students who began in 2026 to budget for annual increases of up to 8 per cent. Meanwhile, some British universities had withdrawn admission offers to Nigerian, Pakistani and Bangladeshi applicants over concerns of breaching stricter visa sponsorship requirements. Home Office figures showed that Nigeria received 26,060 sponsored study visas in the year ending June 2026, behind China with 86,368 and India with 82,523. Pakistan recorded 19,600, while Bangladesh got about 8,800. For Nigerian students, who form one of UK’s largest international cohorts, the charge could translate to higher tuition. The Department for Education data further showed that Nigerian students generated £1.7 billion in UK higher education export revenue in 2024, compared with £5.3 billion from India and £4.9 billion from China. Overall, international students generated an estimated £23.9 billion. Birmingham City University has already raised fees for continuing international students by 2 per cent for 2026-2027, with further 3.5 per cent planned for 2027-2028. The University of Bath has advised overseas students who began in 2026 to budget for annual increases of up to 8 per cent. Meanwhile, some British universities had withdrawn admission offers to Nigerian, Pakistani and Bangladeshi applicants over concerns of breaching stricter visa sponsorship requirements. item.title: Niger miners’ deaths: Committee recommends N1.4bn compensation, dismissal of personnel
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi & Enitan Abdultawab The independent ministerial committee investigating the recent deaths of 33 persons in the custody of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC in Minna, Niger State, has recommended compensation amounting to N1.4 billion to families of the victims. In the Executive Summary by the chairman of the Committee, Jonathan Kure, on Tuesday in Abuja when he presented the report to the Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, the committee, which said the deaths were “entirely preventable”, also recommended summary dismissal of personnel whose actions directly caused the deaths of the suspects. It partly reads, “The committee recommends a restitution of the NSCDCD in order to carry out their reforms. The NDSCD also recommends a restitutive package, a compensation of 30m for each of the 33 bereaved families and 10m to each of the 41 survivors, representing a total compensation package of 1.4 billion naira.” “Additional measures include educational support for dependents of deceased victims, medical rehabilitation of survivors, psychological support for affected families, and a formal apology by the federal government.” It recommended administrative sanctions for personnel who failed in their duties but whose actions or inactions were not directly responsible for the deaths. It added that “fatalities resulted from environmental asphyxia caused by oroloneged confinement in a severely overcrowded cell aggravated by heat stress and dehydration.” According to the committee, the operation which led to the arrest of the suspects was without an “operational order” or approval from the national headquarters of the NSCDC. Total Connected Load: 375 kW Solar PV Capacity: 590 kWp (Kilowatt-peak) System Type: Hybrid Solar PV System with intelligent energy storage (BESS) and smart integration with the existing grid (AEDC) and diesel generators. Verifiable evidence of at least three (3) similar commercial/industrial (C&I) solar projects of 300kWp and above successfully executed in Nigeria within the last five (5) years (include award letters and job completion certificates). Company profile containing CVs of key technical personnel, including COREN-registered engineers or certified solar installers. SITE VISIT A mandatory pre-bid site inspection and clarification meeting will hold on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 10:00 AM at the project site in Utako, Abuja. 7.
